Hi Alex —

Attached are the benchmark results from the quick run we discussed. High-level summary up front:

- Hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (dedicated)
- Model variant: redwood-open-medium (quantized INT8)
- Prefill token length: tested 512 and 1024 tokens

Numbers (median of 5 runs per slice):
- 512 tokens: p50=48ms, p95=98ms, p99=138ms; throughput (single-request QPS) ~20 qps without batching, ~120 qps at batch size = 8 (with continuous batching).
- 1024 tokens: p50=85ms, p95=160ms, p99=240ms; throughput ~9 qps no-batch, ~55 qps at batch size = 8.

Notes:
- These tests used prefix/KV cache reuse for repeated conversation patterns; cold-starts will be higher by ~20–30% for p95/p99.
- Quantization to INT8 reduced memory footprint and improved throughput; measured latency impact on p95 was ~5–10% compared to FP16 in this workload.
- Batch sizing yields better amortized cost but can increase tail latency — we recommend adaptive batching with a 50ms jitter window for UI workloads.

Attached files include the raw run logs and the exact launch configs. Link to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-benchmarks

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 20-min technical walk-through with Dylan to review the configs and map them to your production traffic shape (can do early next week).
- If the numbers look reasonable, we can prepare a small pilot environment for you to run tests on your real prompts.

Would Monday or Tuesday morning PST work for a short call? Happy to coordinate times — looping Dylan here so he can pick a slot.
